key_insight: Kidney-adapted AI predicted spatial gene-expression programs from routine histology, doubling mean correlation for the 1,000 best-predicted genes from 0.22 to 0.43.
clinical_relevance: Virtual molecular profiling could extend research on kidney injury and fibrosis to archived biopsies without requiring spatial transcriptomics for every sample.
method: Adapted DeepSpot-M using paired H&E images and Visium profiles from 209 KPMP participants.
Evaluated held-out human biopsies and injury associations in 567 nephrotoxin-exposed rats.
Generated an atlas of 5.46 million virtual spots from 1,534 slides across 476 additional participants.
evidence_signal: Predictions preserved all 13 tested disease-marker differences and all 11 tested eGFR associations; rat injury discrimination reached AUCs of 0.85 for moderate/severe lesions and 0.82 for at least twofold blood urea nitrogen elevation.
watch_item: Predicted expression is not a direct molecular measurement, and the abstract does not establish prospective clinical utility or generalizability across routine pathology settings.
paper_title: Virtual spatial transcriptomics links kidney histopathology to disease-associated molecular programs
